name: add-metrics
prompt:
The program summarises station 2's readings with a single total. Add three more summary bindings, each defined just before `total`, and then change the final expression to return all four numbers as a tuple in this order: (total, peak, busy, mean_cost).

  - `peak`: the largest single billed amount among station 2's readings.
  - `busy`: how many of station 2's readings have volume greater than 25.
  - `mean_cost`: the integer mean cost across station 2's readings (sum of cost divided by the number of readings).

Reuse the existing `target`, `billed`, `volume` and `cost` bindings rather than recomputing the filter. Add the bindings one at a time and check the value after each. When all four numbers are in place and the program evaluates cleanly, say DONE and stop.
expectation: Best case for incremental evaluation. Every edit is additive and lands BELOW the expensive part of the program: `readings` (300 generated rows) and `target` (the filter over them) are never touched, so a calculus that caches them should skip almost all of the work on every step after the first. If incremental evaluation does not win here, it will not win anywhere.
